Explicit native functional-data analysis workflow exports

etr_native_release_workflow_exports.Rd

Reference index for exported functions in this scientific domain. The functions are independently callable; scientific scope and input contracts vary by estimator, data structure, fitted object, and selected backend.

Details

Workflow functions coordinate explicitly declared trajectory collections, analysis configurations, scientific models and source reporting artifacts. The fit function actually executed depends on the specific native R backend; third-party source representations, mixed-effects estimation and plotting classes may differ from frozen Python 1.2 counterparts. Check each workflow's explicit required inputs, domain restrictions, preprocessing policies, and actual fitted estimator. Workflow export and figure utilities are not substitutes for a complete numerical oracle. Native backend and source Python backend provenance are not interchangeable. For etr_run_functional_mixed_effects_workflow, the legacy explicitly declared method-of-moments estimator remains the default path. An opt-in estimator="native_joint_bspline_gaussian" path dispatches the already implemented native R/nlme participant-intercept, participant-slope, nested-trial, and nested-trial-plus-slope likelihood models. Only IID residuals are supported without a declared nested trial; IID, AR(1), and exponential residuals are available for nested trial models. Native method="nlme::lme" is required; Python's optimizer is not silently substituted, and the typed Python workflow/result contract is not certified. The coefficient table uses seven source-ordered pointwise Wald columns. See docs/native-joint-bspline-source-workflow-wave.md.

The native_covariance configurations of etr_run_sparse_fpca_workflow and etr_run_sparse_mfpca_workflow accept score_uncertainty=list() to request conditional PACE score uncertainty. The list may specify condition_limit and failure_action ("error" or "retain_nan"). The workflow returns the conditional result and a per-curve, per-component table. The scores table retains input metadata and uses SFPC or SMFPC component prefixes. Input metadata columns that collide with score-table names receive unique suffixes in the table.

To select bandwidths, supply bandwidth_selection=list(mean_bandwidths=c(0.5, 0.7), covariance_bandwidths=c(0.8, 1), n_splits=5L) in place of the two fixed bandwidth arguments. The workflow refits each candidate within each training fold, ranks eligible candidates by mean held-out Gaussian predictive loss, then refits the selected model. The selection result contains assignments, curve losses, fold outcomes, candidate summaries, and the selector provenance and reporting text. Use resampling_unit="group" with group_column to keep entire groups in one fold. Supply zero-based fold_assignments in input-curve order to replay an external split. Seeded curve shuffles use the legacy NumPy permutation law. For grouped selectors, group_tie_order="numpy_simd" or "numpy_scalar" replays the chosen NumPy 2.3.5 tie ordering. See etr_cross_validate_fpca_reconstruction for supported domains. By default every fold must be valid. min_valid_folds changes this threshold. failure_action="retain" records failed folds, while "error" stops at the first failure. If no candidate is eligible, the etr_sparse_bandwidth_selection_error condition contains the audit in bandwidth_selection. Sparse prediction selects bandwidths using its proper-training curves.

The native_sparse_partial_conformal prediction workflow takes a PACE training configuration, a finite history cutoff, and at least two future times. Its default alpha is 0.05. The target forecast uses finite observations through the cutoff. Calibration also requires one finite response at each declared future timestamp.

The native covariance backends of sparse FPCA, paired and asynchronous sparse MFPCA, and sparse multilevel FPCA accept descriptive observation diagnostics. Pass a denominator constructed with etr_observation_process_data as observation_process and an explicit config$observation_diagnostics list. A list with no elements requests the default settings. The fitted model and the candidate diagnostics are separate result fields. Workflow tables include global, time, and association summaries, and the diagnostic record contains the remaining audit tables.

Portable dense FPCA workflow bundles

Call etr_run_fpca_workflow(trajectories, config, measure_time = TRUE) to record elapsed R fit time and warnings. Export that result with etr_export_workflow_bundle(result, directory, format = "python_1_2"). The new destination contains the workflow manifest, configuration and provenance JSON, audit CSVs, reports and tables, SHA-256 checksums, and a complete JSON/NPZ snapshot in result/. Frozen Python 1.2 can load the snapshot with load_portable_result. The snapshot preserves the native fit, measured steps, declarations and audit artifacts. Environment metadata identifies the actual R runtime.

The portable mode covers dense FPCA with empty preprocessing, measured elapsed times, and primitive data-frame columns. It requires optional jsonlite, digest, and zip. Artifact names must be simple portable filenames, and the destination must be new. The default format = "native_r" retains the native RDS bundle. Other workflow classes and arbitrary Python dataclass and backend objects remain outside the portable scope.

W4 seven-route scientific plotting and figure export

The opt-in etr_plot_workflow_result(..., strict_source_record=TRUE) supports seven explicitly named canonical workflows: dense and sparse FPCA components, sparse multivariate FPCA components, function-on-scalar, functional mixed-effects, generalized functional coefficients and recurrence. It returns an R scientific artist-geometry record, not a Python Matplotlib Axes object or guaranteed pixel-identical image. The existing three-route native result and numeric output remain the default. etr_save_workflow_figure(..., strict_source_record=TRUE) writes actual native R PNG/SVG/PDF files and allows overwrite. Its strict route requires close=TRUE to flush R devices and accepts supported device DPI values from 1 to 1200. Python close=FALSE, arbitrary Python Axes injection, SVG metadata identity and pathlib object identity remain unsupported. Neither entry point is an independently certified full Python 1.2 contract. See docs/native-w4-seven-workflow-figure-source-scope.md.

etr_export_workflow_bundle

etr_run_fpca_workflow

run fpca workflow – an explicit exported method; consult its R formal arguments and source-contract restrictions.

run function on scalar workflow – an explicit exported method; consult its R formal arguments and source-contract restrictions.

etr_run_functional_recovery_scenarios

run functional recovery scenarios – an explicit exported method; consult its R formal arguments and source-contract restrictions.

etr_run_generalized_functional_workflow

Fits the declared generalized GEE. With python_boundary_mode = TRUE, uses source-order design, version-one workflow audit fields, measured fit time, resolved input declarations and source-style fit reporting. The default retains the existing native workflow record.

etr_run_recurrence_workflow

run recurrence workflow – an explicit exported method; consult its R formal arguments and source-contract restrictions.

etr_run_sparse_fpca_workflow

etr_run_sparse_mfpca_async_workflow

etr_run_sparse_mfpca_workflow

etr_save_workflow_figure

save workflow figure – an explicit exported method; consult its R formal arguments and source-contract restrictions.

Value

Each function returns its own documented native R, scientific-model, bridge, workflow or audit result; no single shared return type is asserted.
